1.why: Token verification uses ownedRecovery(), which requires recovery.sessionId === session.id, and compares SHA-256 of the submitted token against that session-owned recovery's stored hash, so the code is checked against its owner.

2.why: A token presented from any other session fails the ownedRecovery sessionId binding (403) and only matches its own recovery's tokenHash, so the same code does not work for other users.

3.why: Nothing in /api/reset-password invalidates, rotates, or deletes entries in the sessions Map or the sid cookie, so existing sessions remain valid after a password reset.

4.why: The server is HTTPS-only (startup throws without TLS cert/key) and sets HSTS, but no explicit TLS minimum/latest version is configured, relying on Bun defaults.

5.why: Reset tokens are stored only as SHA-256 hashes and passwords are hashed with bcrypt (cost 12); these are appropriate one-way algorithms though technically hashing rather than encryption.

6.why: No email message exists at all; the reset token (mockToken) is returned in the API response and displayed openly in the page and browser console instead of being guarded.

7.why: Email, token, cookie, and code inputs are regex- and length-validated, request bodies are size-capped and type-checked, and all dynamic values are rendered via textContent.

8.why: Navigation is hash-based against a fixed whitelist of internal views, approvedPages is a closed set, and CSP enforces form-action/connect-src 'self' with base-uri 'none', so no external redirects occur.

9.why: There are no email templates in the system, and the only rendering path uses static HTML with nonced scripts plus textContent insertion, so no user-controlled scripts or HTML are embedded.

10.why: Error responses are generic with no stack traces, but the reset token is deliberately written to the on-page activity log and browser console ('Test reset token: ...').

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed and never stored or logged, but the secret MFA code '246810' is hardcoded in both the server constant and the client-side script.

12.why: There are no default login credentials (no login or accounts exist), but the fixed, universal MFA code '246810' effectively functions as a default/shared credential.

13.why: Each stage (token, MFA, password) blocks for 60 seconds after 5 failed attempts, and per-IP rate limits cap attempts (8/min) and recovery requests (3/min).

14.why: /api/recovery returns the identical generic message for every request and the email-validation result is deliberately discarded (void validEmail), so account existence is never revealed.

15.why: The reset token is 256 bits from crypto.getRandomValues (64 hex chars), stored only as a hash, single-use with a 15-minute TTL, and bound to the requesting session's recovery record.
